criteria.name: Cost when the environment changes
criteria.basis: Measured: share of the avoidable extra cost removed, between the design-year tree without a monitor (0) and the lower bound that knows the change in advance (5); mean of six scenarios.

criteria.name: Optimality certificate
criteria.basis: F1: robust tree not proven, gap reported. F2: 3 of 3 library trees proven optimal; the monitor is tested, not proven. F3: confidence intervals only.

criteria.name: Readability
criteria.basis: Measured: rules an operator must read (F1 4, F2 19, F3 26); 5 for at most 6, 4 for at most 12, 3 for at most 20.

criteria.name: Works without a model
criteria.basis: Judgement: F1 and F2 need the transition model of each environment; F3 needs only a simulator.

criteria.name: Scaling with the state space
criteria.basis: Measured: the plain mixed-integer program was solved to optimality in 2 of 3 sizes within 240 s; the simulator search took under 1 s at the largest size and ended 1% above the bound.

criteria.name: Reuse of the existing optimisation model
criteria.basis: Judgement: F1 is one mixed-integer program; F2 adds one per environment and a monitor; F3 is new code.

final.text: After the review the best-scoring framework was combined with the monitor: the robust tree runs by default and a specialised tree takes over only on a heat or wind-lull label from a leaf that is at least 90% pure. This does not lower the mean extra cost over the lower bound (212 against 21 GWh per year), so the page applies the best-scoring framework unchanged and uses the monitor as an alarm only.

scores.summary: Three ways to extend the model were built and scored on this case. F1 scores highest (69 of 100), ahead of F2 (50) and F3 (48). Two criteria are measured on the simulations, two on the solver runs, and two are judgements, marked as such. Weights are a choice; the table lets a reader change them.
scores.sensitivity_note: Exact expected cost in GWh per year. 'Cost of not selecting' is the robust tree minus the tree built for that environment. With 8 block-splits the three differences sum to 0 GWh; with 10 block-splits the three differences sum to 205 GWh; with 12 block-splits the three differences sum to 2,350 GWh.
scores.scaling_note: Heat objective, depth-2 tree, plain mixed-integer program without a starting solution, time limit 240 s. Longer memory multiplies the states by three each step; the tests of the tree stay the same. The local search with exact evaluation took 1, 1, 1 s and the dynamic-programming bound 0.01, 0.01, 0.07 s at the three sizes.
